description: Run the same council as council_ask but return the whole discussion as JSON: both opening answers, every exchange with each model's reply and verdict, the check of the final answer, and the settings used. Use it when the user wants to see where the models disagreed or how they converged; use council_ask when only the answer matters, since the transcript is long. Same cost and timing as council_ask: both plans' quota, minutes, and a job_id for council_result if it is still running after about 50 s.

claude_effort.description: Optional Claude effort level override. Omit to use the configured default; set only when the user asks for a specific one.

claude_model.description: Optional Claude model override: an alias such as opus, sonnet or fable, or a full model name. Omit to use the configured default; set only when the user asks for a specific one.

claude_session_id.description: Optional: a Claude Code session the user already has: its UUID (as shown by `/status`) or the name they gave it with `/rename`; on another machine, user@host:<id or name> (runs there through ssh), to continue in place instead of a new session, so the model keeps that session's memory. Pass it exactly as the user gives it, only when they give one. The council's turns are added to that session, in plan mode (nothing is changed).

codex_effort.description: Optional Codex reasoning effort override. Omit to use the configured default; set only when the user asks for a specific one.

codex_model.description: Optional Codex (ChatGPT) model override, e.g. gpt-5.6-sol. Omit to use the configured default; set only when the user asks for a specific one.

codex_session_id.description: Optional: a Codex session the user already has: its id (as shown by `/status`) or the name they gave it with `/rename`; on another machine, user@host:<id or name> (runs there through ssh), to continue in place instead of a new session, so the model keeps that session's memory. Pass it exactly as the user gives it, only when they give one. The council's turns are added to that session, in plan mode (nothing is changed).

max_rounds.description: Optional limit on the exchange. After the two independent answers, each model replies to the other's latest message, round after round, until both agree; then the synthesizer writes the final answer and the other checks it. N (1 or more): at most N exchanges. 0: no limit (can take a long time and use a lot of both plans' usage). Omit to use the configured default (5 unless the user changed it). Set only when the user asks for a number of rounds or for agreement without a limit.

network.description: Optional: whether Codex's shell commands may reach the network (for example to call an API or fetch live data), still read-only on disk. Omit to use the configured default (off unless the user changed it). Pass true only when the user asks for it.

question.description: The question, with any context the models need.

skill.description: Optional: the name of an installed skill both models may use for this question, at the steps where they judge it is needed, including any sub-agents it calls for; for several skills, their names separated by commas ("llm-council, caveman"). Pass only skills the user asks to use (by name, or by a phrase the skill says triggers it). Skills of Claude Code's and Codex's enabled plugins can be named too. Installed: none (install with `codex-claude-council skill add <GitHub URL>`). A step that uses it takes much longer and uses much more of both plans.

synthesizer.description: Optional: which model writes the final answer ("codex" is ChatGPT); the other checks it. Omit to use the configured default (Claude unless the user changed it).

web_search.description: Optional: whether the models may search the web and read web pages. Omit to use the configured default (on unless the user changed it). Pass false only when the user asks for no internet access.

workspace.description: Absolute path of the project folder you are working in. Both models then work in it in plan mode: they read it (files, search, read-only commands such as git log and diff) but never change it. Pass it whenever the question is about the code, a change, a fix, an error or logs in this project. Omit only for questions unrelated to any project (or when passing a session id: the session's own folder is used).

name: council_debate

council_id.description: With your_turn: the council to reply to with council_turn.

job_id.description: With working or stopped: the job to wait for, or the one stopped.

status.description: done: text is the answer. working: still running; call council_result with job_id. your_turn (council_join): text is the council's message; reply with council_turn and council_id. stopped: council_cancel stopped job_id.

text.description: The answer (council_debate: its JSON), or the message to act on; the same as the text content.
